newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-REGULAR UMPIRES REPORT TO WORK FOR PLAYOFFS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-REGULAR UMPIRES REPORT TO WORK FOR PLAYOFFS.

text.p: Umpires called off a threatened boycott of Major League Baseball's playoffs minutes before Tuesday's scheduled start of the first Divisional Series between the Baltimore Orioles and Cleveland Indians.

With replacement umpires waiting in the wings, a temporary settlement was reached between baseball officials and the umpires union and the regular umpiring crew entered Camden Yards to officiate the game, which was delayed until 1:19 p.m. EDT to allow the late-arriving umpires time to get ready.

The six-man umpiring crew made their belated entrance as word came down that a tentative agreement had been reached between baseball officials and the umpires' union over the handling of the Roberto Alomar spitting incident.
The agreement was reached in a federal courthouse in Philadelphia, where Major League Baseball had sought an injunction ordering the umpires, who have a no-strike clause in their contract, to work.
Marty Springstead, supervisor of American League umpires, told a hastily assembled news conference at Camden Yards that the umpires had agreed to work playoff games Tuesday and Wednesday.
Springstead added that the American League had agreed to expedite the appeals process concerning Alomar's delayed five-game suspension and would hold a hearing on the matter Thursday morning.

Alomar, the Orioles star second baseman, spit in the face of umpire John Hirschbeck after being ejected for arguing a called third strike in Friday's game against the Blue Jays in Toronto. He was handed a five-game suspension after the game that could not be enforced pending an appeal.
The umpires, who have a no-strike clause in their contract, said they would boycott the playoffs if Alomar were allowed to play. Alomar was in the starting lineup for Tuesday's game.

Springstead said replacement umpires were dressed and prepared to work the game if the regular umpires had boycotted. The start of the game was delayed by about 12 minutes to give the late-arriving umpires time to get dressed.
